items.title: WAL-G 3.0.10 released
items.summary: The WAL-G team is pleased to announce the release of WAL-G 3.0.10.WAL-G is an open-source backup and recovery tool for PostgreSQL,Apache Cloudberry, MySQL/MariaDB, MongoDB, Redis, and otherdatabases.The main new PostgreSQL feature iswal-send. It serves archivedWAL over PostgreSQL's streaming replication protocol, allowing standbysand pg_receivewal to read WAL directly from object storage and follownew segments as they arrive.Other PostgreSQL improvements include:Continuous WAL archival in daemon mode: the pipeline keeps working  between requests, and retained lookahead reduces directory scanning  (#2697,  #2698).Optional backup-push --wait-for-archive: WAL-G waits for all WAL  segments required by the backup to reach the selected backup storage  before publishing the backup as complete  (#2722).Backup-name reservation before upload, protecting against concurrent  reuse of the same name  (#2707).WAL prefetch files are published only after a successful download  (#2696), and WAL source files  are closed after upload failures  (#2695).Standard X/X LSN notation in catchup-push --from-lsn  (#2643).S3 support now uses AWS SDK v2 and adds configurable request timeouts,retryable error codes, and checksum settings. Backup copying can useserver-side S3 copy and configurable transfer concurrency.Greenplum and Cloudberry improvements include per-backup accounting forshared AO/AOCS/PAX storage and fixes to segment backup, restore, and copyoperations.One behavior change to note: permanent backups remain protected fromretention-based deletion, but an explicit delete target can now removethem (#2808).WAL-G v3.0.10 is available for download, along with the full releasenotes, on ourGitHub releases page.Have a nice day!

items.title: pgjumbo: a new free desktop client for PostgreSQL
items.summary: pgjumbo is a new desktop client for PostgreSQL 12+, free to use, for Windows, macOS and Linux, with query, data and administration tools.pgjumbo connects to PostgreSQL 12+, including Amazon Aurora and RDS with IAM authentication, directly, over SSL or through an SSH tunnel. Installers are available for Windows (x64 and ARM64), macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) and Linux (AppImage, .deb and .rpm).Version 1.0.2 includes:An object explorer and inspector with each object's CREATE script, statistics and dependencies.A Query Tool with completion, syntax errors from PostgreSQL's own parser as you type, parameters, EXPLAIN as a table or a diagram, and results that can be sorted, filtered, compared and exported.A data editor that shows the statements before it saves them.Backup and restore built on pg_dump, pg_dumpall and pg_restore: choosing objects and rows, server backups as a folder of archives, reading an archive's contents before restoring, and restoring into a new database.Maintenance: what each table needs and what holds VACUUM back, VACUUM, ANALYZE and REINDEX as reviewed steps with progress, and autovacuum settings per table.Server activity, configuration, roles and privileges, logs, replication, pg_cron jobs and LISTEN/NOTIFY.Changes to objects are shown as SQL and reviewed before they run, and on servers marked Production, destructive statements ask for confirmation first.Download pgjumbo · Release notes for 1.0.2

items.title: pgSherpa: a free PostgreSQL monitoring companion for macOS
items.summary: CortexRidge has released pgSherpa, a free desktop companion for PostgreSQL on macOS, now available on the Mac App Store.pgSherpa sits in a corner of the screen and polls one or more PostgreSQL servers (PostgreSQL 12 to 18). When something needs attention it says so in a sentence, with the rows behind it:Health: lock-wait chains, long-running and idle-in-transaction sessions, replication lag and replication slots, vacuum and transaction ID wraparound, connection limits.Security: the server's version compared with the latest PostgreSQL minor release and the CVEs fixed since, plus configuration such as SSL, MD5 passwords and superuser count.Cloud: backups, failovers, maintenance windows and replicas for DigitalOcean Managed Databases, Supabase and Amazon RDS / Aurora PostgreSQL, read from the provider's API.SQL: a query box with PostgreSQL completion and \h syntax help for the server's own version. Every statement runs in a read-only transaction unless the user switches it to write.Reports: ready-made views of pg_stat_activity, pg_locks, pg_stat_statements, vacuum progress, indexes and replication.pgSherpa needs only a role with pg_monitor. It installs no extension and no agent on the server, and it has no account and no telemetry; passwords and keys stay in the macOS Keychain.It runs on macOS 12 or later, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs.Mac App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6833955115More information: https://cortexridge.com/
